I don't have shell or command execution tools available in this environment — my tools are limited to filesystem operations (within allowed directories), a browser, a read-only SQL query tool, and Notion API access. None of these can modify `/etc/sysctl.conf` or invoke `sysctl`.

To run that yourself on the target Linux host:

```bash
echo "net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_ra=2" | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.conf
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1
```

A couple of notes on the command itself:
- `accept_ra=2` is the correct setting when you also enable forwarding, since by default the kernel ignores Router Advertisements once forwarding is on. Setting it to 2 keeps RA processing enabled.
- `sysctl -w` only changes the running value. To make forwarding persistent across reboots, also append it to the config:
  ```bash
  echo "net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1" | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.conf
  ```
- To reload all persisted settings: `sudo sysctl -p`.

If you'd like, I can write these lines into a file within an allowed directory (e.g., a snippet for `/etc/sysctl.d/99-ipv6.conf`) that you can then copy into place.
